cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel and David's son, has more riches and wisdom than any king on earth (1 Kings 10:23). The man made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones (1 Kings 10:27). STONES, friend! Then this chapter opens with the one word nobody wants to hear: however.

cards.question: Solomon loves the daughter of Pharaoh, king of Egypt. But she's not the only one. What else does Solomon love?

cards.text: We're talking women of Moab, Ammon, Edom and Sidon, plus Hittite women. That's not a guest list, friend. That's a MAP.

cards.question: The LORD had already told the Israelites something about these nations: You must not ___ with them.
Why did the LORD tell the Israelites not to intermarry with those nations?

answers.text: They would turn Israel's hearts after their gods
They would carry off Israel's silver and gold
They would bring their armies into Israel

cards.question: Even with that warning from the LORD, Solomon keeps his distance from these women.

cards.text: Now the numbers: seven hundred wives of royal birth and three hundred concubines. Friend, I lose track of ONE timer in my own bakery, and this man has seven HUNDRED anniversaries.

cards.question: When Solomon grows old, his wives turn his heart after other gods. He isn't wholeheartedly devoted to the LORD the way ___ had been.

cards.text: And the text gets specific. Solomon follows Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, and Milcom, the abomination of the Ammonites.

cards.question: Solomon is following Ashtoreth and Milcom. How does the text sum up what he's doing?

answers.text: He did evil in the sight of the LORD
He made peace in the sight of the nations
He did justice in the sight of his people

cards.text: This isn't tucked in the back of a junk drawer, friend. Solomon starts building on a hill east of Jerusalem.

cards.question: What does Solomon build on that hill east of Jerusalem?

answers.text: A high place for Chemosh and Molech
A storehouse for his gold and ivory
A stable for his horses and chariots

cards.question: Solomon builds places like that only for his wives from Moab and Ammon.

cards.text: His foreign wives burn incense and sacrifice to their gods. And now the LORD grows angry with Solomon.

cards.question: Why does the LORD grow angry with Solomon?

answers.text: His heart had turned away from the LORD
He had spent too much of Israel's gold
He had grown too proud of his throne

cards.question: This is the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to Solomon ___.

cards.text: An angel showed up in my drawer ONE time, and I'm still telling everybody about it. And this same God had warned Solomon plainly not to follow other gods.
Solomon didn't keep that command. So the LORD speaks to him: because Solomon hasn't kept His covenant and His statutes, something is coming.

cards.question: The LORD tells Solomon He will tear the ___ away from him.
Who will the LORD give the kingdom to once He tears it away from Solomon?

cards.text: But even here, there's mercy. It comes for the sake of Solomon's father David.

cards.question: For David's sake, the LORD says He won't tear the kingdom away during Solomon's lifetime.

cards.text: Instead, He'll tear it out of the hand of Solomon's son. And even then, He won't take the whole thing.

cards.question: How many tribes will the LORD give to Solomon's son?
The LORD leaves Solomon's son that tribe for the sake of His servant ___ and for the sake of ___, the city He has chosen.

cards.text: And that's where we'll set this batch down to cool, friend. Trust me, this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'Solomon... (1 Kings 10:23).' 'The man made silver... (1 Kings 10:27).' 'STONES, friend!' 'Then this chapter opens...' It needs to be cut to 3 or fewer.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The setup 'But she's not the only one' points to more women, which rules out 'Many foreign horses' and 'Many foreign ships' before the baker picks. The question gives the answer away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'This isn't tucked in the back of a junk drawer' before anything has been named, so 'This' points to nothing. The joke also rests on an idea the card never says (that the building was out in the open), so it doesn't click right away.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: 'Solomon builds places like that' points back to the high place for Chemosh and Molech from the previous card, which is no longer on screen. The question should name what was built.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'thrice' sounds old-fashioned and Bible-like next to 'twice' and 'once', so the answers don't sound alike.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The closing line 'And that's where we'll set this batch down to cool, friend. Trust me, this story is NOT done.' copies the doc's example ('And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.') nearly word for word instead of being a new line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: This last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse, but it cites 1 Kings 11:13, which was already asked on card 15. The citation rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, and this card tells none.
findings.question: What should the verses field be for a story card that is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verses: the passage's last verse, the verses of the previous card, or something else?
